cards.power: Picture the future as a page with room left on it, not a poster on a wall.
cards.lore: Protopia is the idea that the future is a process of slow, incremental improvement you participate in.
cards.gradeReason: Painterly and immediately imagistic — you are already holding the pencil.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: eager beaver gripping oversized pencil, blank notebook open. Mood: focused readiness.

cards.power: Draw the next step in pencil. Pencil means you expect to be wrong and stay anyway.
cards.lore: The ability to correct beats the appearance of certainty.
cards.gradeReason: A single tool choice IS the performance. No translation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: grinning raccoon erasing a blueprint mid-sketch. Mood: gleeful impermanence.

cards.power: Make the first version bad on purpose. Bad is how you know it is real.
cards.lore: Starting before you are ready produces better results than waiting for a perfect plan.
cards.gradeReason: Permission plus method plus proof — clearest creative invite in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: possum proudly holding a chaotic crossed-out treasure map. Mood: unashamed momentum.

cards.power: Do not finish it. Improve it once, then leave it better and open.
cards.lore: Continuous small improvement treats work as never finished, compounding into large change.
cards.gradeReason: The loop is the action. Player becomes the woodpecker pecking BETTER into the tree.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: red-crested woodpecker drilling BETTER into tree bark repeatedly. Mood: relentless iterative joy.

cards.power: Find one broken thing close enough to touch.
cards.lore: Reframing a vast problem as a specific, local, finishable task restores the sense that action is possible.
cards.gradeReason: Spatial and immediate — you look around the room right now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: iguana in tool belt oiling a hinge while city burns behind. Mood: focused calm amid chaos.

cards.power: Choose a repair you can finish this week, not a revolution you can only announce.
cards.lore: A series of small wins builds momentum and evidence that larger change is possible.
cards.gradeReason: Binary choice — finish vs. announce — forces immediate behavior selection.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: squirrel with goggles writing a short to-do list, acorn as anchor. Mood: practical determination.

cards.power: Accept that small fixes do not trend. They just hold.
cards.lore: Maintenance and repair are systematically undervalued because they are undramatic.
cards.gradeReason: Mindset acceptance not performance trigger — needs a moment of internal processing first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: turtle in raincoat trimming a fence in the rain, unbothered. Mood: quiet persistence.

cards.power: One repair a week is fifty-two a year. Nobody clapped, and the place is different.
cards.lore: Small consistent improvements accumulate non-linearly over time, outperforming heroic one-offs.
cards.gradeReason: Nobody clapped is instantly embodied — invisible heroism becomes a complete identity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: badger with ruler laying checkmarks across a growing grid of tiles. Mood: quiet compound pride.

cards.power: Before reacting, take the one breath the feed is built to deny you.
cards.lore: A deliberate slow exhale activates the parasympathetic system, a fast physiological route from reaction back into thinking.
cards.gradeReason: Physiologically immediate — reader is already breathing. The card is its own performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: sloth hanging from branch exhaling a slow blue cloud over a frantic city below. Mood: sovereign calm.

cards.power: Breathe low enough to think. The nervous system votes with oxygen.
cards.lore: Reclaiming attention begins with regulating the physical body that carries it.
cards.gradeReason: Physical instruction plus biological fact — the body is the stage and it is already on.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: glowing whale diving deep underwater surrounded by tiny luminous fish. Mood: deep sovereign intelligence.

cards.power: Let stillness feel like falling behind. It is actually catching up to yourself.
cards.lore: Brief disengagement and mind-wandering support consolidation, so the empty moment is where understanding forms.
cards.gradeReason: Reframe of stillness is smart but internal — surrender required before performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: capybara sitting alone on park bench, one lightbulb forming above its head. Mood: peaceful latent insight.

cards.power: Place attention on purpose. Take one second back, then another.
cards.lore: Agency over attention is foundational, making the reclaimed second the smallest unit of freedom.
cards.gradeReason: Micro-action, right now, one second — smallest possible threshold for embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: chameleon pressing a HERE button with one precise toe, gears behind it. Mood: quiet decisive agency.

cards.power: Authority is overrated, proximity is underrated. Ask the one who actually does the thing.
cards.lore: Real know-how is tacit knowledge, learned by doing and living in practitioners.
cards.gradeReason: Clear action but needs a specific person nearby — context-dependent performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: boar in overalls leaning over fence sharing a wrench with porcupine mechanic. Mood: no-nonsense neighborly trust.

cards.power: Trade the forecaster's confidence for the neighbor's callus.
cards.lore: Skills and knowledge are sustained and passed on within communities of practice bound by shared doing.
cards.gradeReason: Strong metaphor but forecaster/callus trade is a frame shift not immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: grizzled chimp handing wrench to young monkey while a diploma fizzles overhead. Mood: earned competence over credentials.

cards.power: Notice that real know-how is often badly dressed and lives three doors down.
cards.lore: Authority signals like polish and credentials can be inversely related to hands-on competence.
cards.gradeReason: An observational reframe — good insight but notice is softer than do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: scruffy capybara being interviewed by tiny clipboard-holding bird about expertise. Mood: inverse credibility amusement.

cards.power: Pass knowledge hand to hand. It cannot be deplatformed.
cards.lore: Knowledge held and taught within a community is robust against single points of failure.
cards.gradeReason: Pass knowledge hand to hand is as physical as it gets — and the punchline seals it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: gang of crows passing a lockpick through many hands in a circle. Mood: conspiratorial solidarity.

cards.power: Turn watching into showing up. Name a time, a place, a task.
cards.lore: Action is far more likely when it is specific and social, converting vague intention into behavior.
cards.gradeReason: Name a time, a place, a task — three exact behaviors, fully embodied immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: frazzled pelican stapling BRING GLOVES flyers to a lamppost. Mood: urgent amateur organizer energy.

cards.power: Split a problem the way your ancestors raised a barn.
cards.lore: Mutual aid is a deep and widespread survival strategy across species, older than money.
cards.gradeReason: Barn-raising metaphor is vivid but requires translation to a current specific problem.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: octopus in denim vest hammering roof beams with all eight arms at once. Mood: ancestral collaborative muscle.

cards.power: Go to the first small, clumsy gathering anyway. Clumsy is the entry fee.
cards.lore: The willingness to tolerate an awkward beginning separates groups that form from groups that stay imagined.
cards.gradeReason: Clumsy is the entry fee is a complete permission slip and performance cue in one.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: pigeon, emu, duck, and crow awkwardly huddled over coffee carafe on bare table. Mood: painfully hopeful first meeting.

cards.power: Build together until the crowd can act, not just feel together.
cards.lore: Communities that self-organize shared resources thicken over repeated cooperation.
cards.gradeReason: Outcome description more than invitation — act vs. feel is sharp but it is a process milestone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: flock of small yellow birds collectively weaving a thick rope around a wooden post. Mood: cumulative collective power.

cards.power: The future you can touch is the next few hours. Start there.
cards.lore: Action only ever occurs in the present, making today the only workable unit of the future.
cards.gradeReason: Start there — two words of complete instruction after a clear frame. Immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: small bat clinging to pocket watch face, wings spread, clock hands at golden hour. Mood: urgent present-tense focus.

cards.power: Trade one perfect someday for one finished today.
cards.lore: A completed small action changes the world more than a large intended one.
cards.gradeReason: Clean binary swap — dung beetle rolling a real ball vs. glowing dream castle. Total clarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: dung beetle in patched jacket pushing a real mud ball away from a holographic dream castle. Mood: grounded over glamour.

cards.power: Accept that today's improvement is small and real. Both are features.
cards.lore: Taking small concrete actions before motivation arrives reliably lifts mood and agency.
cards.gradeReason: Acceptance is the action — but it requires internal reframe before the external move fires.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: moose in flannel shirt sweeping a floor with a broom, coffee cup steaming nearby. Mood: dignified unglamorous effort.

cards.power: Act now, because now is the only place leverage lives.
cards.lore: Agency is structurally located in the now; the past is fixed and the future is unreachable.
cards.gradeReason: True and sharp but leverage lives is philosophical — Act now needs a what attached.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: armored rhino driving a shoulder into a brick, coffee cup steam wafting behind. Mood: irreversible committed force.

cards.power: Treat the stranger as a possible ally with a different toolbox, not a threat.
cards.lore: Humans succeeded as a species through unusual friendliness to non-kin.
cards.gradeReason: Mindset reframe is clear; toolbox metaphor useful but the action is still internal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: spotted hyena and vulture awkwardly exchanging wrenches, meeting eyes cautiously. Mood: wary species-crossing curiosity.

cards.power: Lower the bar to contact. Most cooperation starts embarrassingly small.
cards.lore: Low-stakes contact between groups reliably reduces prejudice.
cards.gradeReason: Lower the bar to contact IS the performance — Hello is already the card in action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: two prickly hedgehogs facing each other, one saying HI in a small speech bubble. Mood: tentative generous first step.

cards.power: Accept that they might not respond. Your nervous system thinks that is death. It is not.
cards.lore: Social rejection registers in the brain like physical pain—an outdated survival alarm.
cards.gradeReason: It is not is a great punchline — but acceptance of non-response requires internal defusing first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: panicked quokka ringing a giant bell alone, black puff of silence around it. Mood: alarm system running on wrong data.

cards.power: Go first. Every ally was a stranger until somebody did.
cards.lore: Reciprocal strategies that begin by cooperating outperform purely defensive ones.
cards.gradeReason: Go first — cleanest action command in the STRANGER section. Logic justifies it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: first tapir in a group extending a leaf to a ghost-outline tapir not yet arrived. Mood: founding cooperative gesture.

cards.power: Run on huh, I wonder, instead of we are doomed or we are saved.
cards.lore: Intrinsic motivation produces better learning and persistence than reward or fear.
cards.gradeReason: Swap the internal voice — player is already running on something. The card reroutes it now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: meerkat in overalls drawing a lush green question mark, wildflowers spiraling from its tip. Mood: fertile investigative wonder.

cards.power: Framed as an experiment, wonder costs less than hope.
cards.lore: Framing situations as experiments reduces the paralysis of needing a guaranteed outcome.
cards.gradeReason: Powerful reframe but requires applying to a specific current situation before it fires.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: platypus in lab coat gleefully pouring neon liquid into overflowing beaker. Mood: permitted mess in service of data.

cards.power: Be wrong a lot. Curiosity treats that as data, not defeat.
cards.lore: Treating mistakes as feedback is what allows iteration to converge on what works.
cards.gradeReason: Be wrong a lot is both permission and action — player gets a new job description immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: fox circling a wrong-answer dog with a red arrow, dog morphs happily into a wolf. Mood: iterative transformation without shame.

cards.power: Let interest expand attention where fear shrinks it.
cards.lore: Positive states like curiosity broaden the range of thoughts and actions a person considers.
cards.gradeReason: Describes the mechanism but does not tell you what to do with your hands right now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: owl bursting from a black dome into a kaleidoscopic mountain landscape. Mood: fear-ceiling breaking open to color.

cards.power: Write down what you actually saw, not what the headline said you would see.
cards.lore: Keeping a direct record over time counters the distortions of memory and media.
cards.gradeReason: Write down what you actually saw — exact physical immediately executable action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: grumpy bear in glasses writing intently in a notebook, surrounded by crumpled newspapers. Mood: stubborn first-person epistemology.

cards.power: Count the whole thing, including the times it worked and nobody noticed.
cards.lore: Attending to base rates corrects the overweighting of vivid, alarming cases.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp insight but count the whole thing needs a current data set to engage with.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: raven chalking tally marks on a wall, one highlighted row that nobody circled. Mood: unfashionable statistical honesty.

cards.power: Keep the notes that argue against you. Those are the valuable ones.
cards.lore: Actively seeking disconfirming evidence separates inquiry from rationalization.
cards.gradeReason: Behavioral but requires having existing notes to keep — depends on prior setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: skeptical goat writing furiously in open book, thought bubble full of crossed-out certainties. Mood: principled self-opposition.

cards.power: Trust a page of your own observations over a year of someone else's predictions.
cards.lore: Personal calibrated records outperform remembered impressions and forecasts.
cards.gradeReason: Requires a personal log to trust — strong frame but depends on prior practice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: elephant examining its own smudged notebook, a glowing crystal ball untouched beside it. Mood: sovereign record-keeper over oracle.

cards.power: Make something with your hands this week. Bread, a fix, a fence.
cards.lore: Craftsmanship connects skill, material, and judgment, building a grounded sense of agency.
cards.gradeReason: Bread, a fix, a fence — three perfect examples collapse the ask to fully specific.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: orangutan kneading dough aggressively on a wooden board, flour cloud around it. Mood: grounded tactile making-joy.

cards.power: Let manual work pull attention out of the loop and back into the room.
cards.lore: Absorbing, skill-matched activity produces flow that displaces rumination.
cards.gradeReason: Process invitation — the outcome is clear but let requires giving up the loop first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: otter whittling a wood figure, cracked phone face-down in wood shavings. Mood: absorbed escape from the feed.

cards.power: Work at the speed of hands. That is not a bug, it is the medicine.
cards.lore: Effortful, slower processes produce deeper learning and satisfaction than frictionless ones.
cards.gradeReason: Reframe of slowness as feature — needs the player to be currently doing something slow.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: snail ascending a mushroom stem in rain, serene face, no hurry at all. Mood: therapeutic deliberate pace.

cards.power: A muscle you use stays yours. Friction is what keeps the grip.
cards.lore: Capacities are maintained through use, resisting the quiet erosion of disuse.
cards.gradeReason: Principle over invitation — grip metaphor is strong but the action is implied not commanded.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: gorilla raising a heavy hammer, arm sinew visible, fire in background. Mood: reclaimed physical capability.

cards.power: Do not storm the front gate. Find the side door nobody guards.
cards.lore: Change often enters through small, low-resistance points rather than direct confrontation.
cards.gradeReason: Find the side door nobody guards — spatially immediate strategic and already half the work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: ferret slipping through a cracked side door marked KEEP OUT, grinning. Mood: cheerful principled infiltration.

cards.power: Run a tiny version. Low stakes, real feedback, no permission needed.
cards.lore: Small reversible experiments let you learn what works at low cost before committing.
cards.gradeReason: No permission needed removes the last excuse — Run a tiny version is the complete task.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: city pigeon with a paint roller laying a tiny crosswalk stripe in the street. Mood: unsanctioned practical prototyping.

cards.power: Improvement often looks like mild disobedience to a stuck system.
cards.lore: Small principled noncompliance is a constructive act when declining to cooperate with a broken rule.
cards.gradeReason: Excellent insight but Improvement often looks like is still description not invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: crow in tactical vest repairing a DO NOT REPAIR panel from behind, tools out. Mood: constructive principled disobedience.

cards.power: Build the working example. One beats a thousand arguments.
cards.lore: A functioning demonstration shifts a debate more than rhetoric does.
cards.gradeReason: Build the working example — exact verb, exact artifact, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: three mice building a spinning waterwheel together, crowd of astonished onlookers. Mood: demonstration ending all discussion.

cards.power: Give up being certain. It is harder than giving up money.
cards.lore: Tolerance of ambiguity is a learnable disposition required for protopia.
cards.gradeReason: Harder than giving up money reframes beautifully but surrender is internal work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: pangolin dropping a cracked boulder labeled CERTAIN, sand spraying on impact. Mood: costly but necessary release.

cards.power: Trade the warm baths of hopeless and handled for the cold shower of it depends on us.
cards.lore: Giving up the relief of certainty is the discomfort protopia asks you to accept.
cards.gradeReason: Abstract warmth metaphor — it depends on us is still a frame not yet an action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: toad choosing between DOOM and SAVED armchairs, a question mark umbrella above in rain. Mood: uneasy agency over comfortable despair.

cards.power: Accept there is no final version. The cost is showing up again next week.
cards.lore: Durable improvement is maintained, not achieved once.
cards.gradeReason: Showing up again next week is behavioral but accept is the real ask — internal before external.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: camel with saddlebags standing before a long calendar, every week marked with a brick. Mood: stolid endless commitment.

cards.power: Pay in certainty and comfort. Get back the wheel the other two decks took.
cards.lore: The trade protopia offers is the discomfort of ongoing uncertainty in exchange for restored agency.
cards.gradeReason: Brilliant exhibition-aware meta-reference — but it is a trade description more than performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: kangaroo stamping PAID on a document labeled Certainty and Comfort, receiving a glowing steering wheel. Mood: deliberate costly bargain.

cards.power: If you can see how it was made, you can remake it. Seams are honesty.
cards.lore: Showing the seams of a system lets people understand, question, and modify it.
cards.gradeReason: Seams are honesty is a beautiful reframe but see how it was made requires something seamed in front of you.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: a toad pointing at its own visible suture lines with a knowing grin. Mood: radical transparency as invitation.

cards.power: If it invites your question instead of closing it, you are in the workshop.
cards.lore: Systems that remain genuinely open to revision are the structural signature of participatory process.
cards.gradeReason: Diagnostic framing is sharp — it is a detection heuristic not an immediate action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: scruffy dog holding a notepad reading YOUR TURN, a warm workshop light behind it. Mood: invitation over conclusion.

cards.power: If there is more than one way forward, it is a future, not a funnel.
cards.lore: The presence of multiple viable paths signals genuine agency.
cards.gradeReason: Funnel vs. future is a killer distinction — but spotting it is observation before action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: ant with backpack examining map showing TUNNEL, OVERPASS, MAZE, BRIDGE, UNKNOWN branches. Mood: genuine-option abundance.

cards.power: The rougher and more inviting it is, the more likely it is yours to edit.
cards.lore: Visible imperfection signals an unfinished thing still open to your hand.
cards.gradeReason: Useful heuristic for identifying opportunity — but it is criteria not a direct invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: paint-splattered moth pressed against a perfect glass cube, wings open. Mood: rough aliveness vs. sealed perfection.

cards.power: Look around the actual room you are in. Find the one thing within arm's reach.
cards.lore: Effective change starts from where you already have leverage and access.
cards.gradeReason: Look around the actual room you are in — spatially immediate, requires no metaphor translation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: striped cat drawing a red circle around a ball of yarn in a chaotic room. Mood: calm leverage-finding amid overwhelm.

cards.power: You do not need the whole future. You need today, one percent better.
cards.lore: Marginal gains, small improvements compounded consistently, produce large results.
cards.gradeReason: One percent better is precisely scaled — player knows exactly what size improvement to make.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: chameleon clicking a combination dial labeled FUTURE one notch forward. Mood: micro-precision over total ambition.

cards.power: Nobody will clap. Start anyway. The clapping was never the point.
cards.lore: Action driven by intrinsic purpose is more durable than action requiring applause.
cards.gradeReason: Start anyway — two-word command plus permission to work without audience. Complete.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: mole emerging from dark earth tunnel, no crowd above, digging on regardless. Mood: intrinsic purpose over approval.

cards.power: Forget the brochure. Ignore the loop. Pick up the pencil.
cards.lore: Agency is recovered by converting the vast question of the future into one workable thing you can do now.
cards.gradeReason: Triple command equals triple embodiment. The deck's premise delivered as pure performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink sketch, aged paper. Subject: giant golden paw gripping an oversized fountain pen, tiny aliens watching in awe. Mood: enormous agency compressed to one tool.

verdict: Deck C is the payoff of the Hannover trilogy. Section headers are knockouts throughout — Finished is for tombstones and Revolutions are brochures are G1 from the first syllable. THE CORE QUESTION is the finest closing card in the Kayfabizarro corpus: Forget the brochure. Ignore the loop. Pick up the pencil. The Worthwhile Bill is brilliantly exhibition-aware, referencing the other two decks by name. One structural note: page 4 (cards 9-12) uses a panoramic format without a visible section header, breaking visual consistency. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For visitors paralyzed by big problems and worse news — 56 cards that convert the overwhelming question of the future into one small, specific, touchable thing you can do this week. No manifesto. Just the pencil.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob rabbit mid-action with chisel, burning Yesterday's News newspaper, smashed VR headset, sketch blueprints — layered and immediately readable
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — FORGET UTOPIA. IGNORE DYSTOPIA. EMBRACE PROTOPIA. — perfect three-part escalating command structure
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — irreverent, chaotic, optimistic — exactly the tone the 56 cards deliver
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — nothing else in the corpus starts with a burning newspaper and a rabbit holding a chisel
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — the triple command is endlessly shareable on its own, completely without the card deck
coverQA.coverNote: Strongest cover of the trilogy. The Yesterday's News newspaper burning buries the past without nostalgia. The smashed VR headset signals rejection of escape. The potted plant smoking a cigarette in the corner is the most FrizzleBob detail in the whole exhibition.

notes: Page 4 (cards 9-12: The Held Breath, The Lower Lung, The Boring Gap, The Reclaimed Second) uses a panoramic flowing layout with numbered card circles (09-12) rather than the standard 2x2 grid with bold section header. Section title was not clearly visible in this format — content suggests a BREATH/ATTENTION theme. This is the only story page without a visible section header; all 13 others follow standard layout. Cards 29 and 50 both carry the name The Open Question — intentional, different sections (CURIOSITY vs. THE TELL). The Worthwhile Bill (card 48) contains an explicit cross-deck meta-reference: the wheel the other two decks took — exhibition placement of all three decks together is essential for this line to land. No RAF dice boxes present. No font artifacts detected.

urgent: Verify page 4 section header is visible or intentionally absent in print — panoramic format breaks visual consistency without it
quickWins: Place all three decks physically adjacent at exhibition — The Worthwhile Bill (card 48) only lands when Decks A and B are nearby
niceToHave: Consider adding section-level card numbering consistently across all pages — page 4 has it (09-12), other pages do not

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: EMBRACE PROTOPIA – Fifty-Six Cards That Trade the Whole Future for the One Percent You Can Reach Today (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

What is the smallest repair you would still be willing to make, and who talked you into calling it too small to count?

You have been holding out for a fix big enough to deserve you. The systemic one, the root-cause one, the one that earns the applause and finally makes the effort worth the embarrassment of having tried. So the small stuff stays undone, because small feels like surrender, and you keep standing in front of a problem sized to flatten anyone who looks at it straight. Here is the part nobody can sell you, because nobody has figured out how to price it: one honest percent, made today and repeated, outruns the heroic rescue that never ships. The boring repair compounds. The ugly draft you actually hand over beats the perfect plan still waiting for a braver week.

This is Social Story Wrestling in the EMBRACE register. You pick up the pencil, perform one small move out loud, and the table decides whether the repair would hold once it leaves the page. Nothing here is laminated. The rough edge is not a flaw you sand off later, it is the handle they left on for you.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Embrace Protopia Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Ugly First Draft (the version that embarrasses you a little is the only one that ever leaves your hands), The Compounding (the quiet arithmetic where one small fix, repeated, beats the grand gesture that never arrives), and The Core Question, the turn the whole wing builds toward, the one that stops asking what the future will be and starts asking what you can improve before the week is out.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no qualifications required, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the part where every card can claim anything until the room calls the bluff. Cut on the dotted lines and play the thing.
- The Action Build: fourteen story pages that move from the first awkward attempt through The Boring Gap and The Reclaimed Second toward The Worthwhile Bill, the card that nods to the other two wings hanging on the wall, and land on the Core Question you carry off the table and into your week.

This is the EMBRACE wing of the Hannover triptych. Forget refuses the rescue fantasy on the left, Ignore walks past the fear machine in the middle, and this wing does the one thing the other two only clear the ground for, which is to make something. Read a column straight down and one question gets three answers. The whole triptych lives at protopians.substack.com. Bring a pencil and start before you are ready.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The future is not won in one heroic stroke. It is compounded, one ugly repair at a time, by whoever refused to wait for permission."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
